input: Coordinate a neighborhood block party for July

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing what is included — food, games, music, decorations, permits — determines how many moving parts the plan needs to cover.
The expected number of attendees and whether there are co-organizers or volunteers dramatically affects logistics, budgeting, and task delegation.
The specific date and time in July affects permit deadlines, vendor availability, and how much planning time remains.
The budget sets hard limits on venue, catering, entertainment, and supplies — the entire plan scales around it.
Whether a street closure permit is needed, and who is responsible for obtaining it, is a critical early action that can block everything else.
The tone and theme (family-friendly, adult-focused, cultural celebration, casual cookout) shapes activity choices, food, and communications.
Understanding what a successful event looks like — turnout, community bonding, fun for kids, smooth execution — helps prioritize tasks correctly.

gold.taskTitle: Coordinate a neighborhood block party in July
gold.taskDescription: Plan and organize a block party for the user's neighborhood, to take place sometime in July.

questions.title: What activities and amenities do you want to include?
questions.description: Determine scope: food, music, games, bounce houses, decorations, etc.

questions.title: How many people are you expecting to attend?
questions.description: Establish the expected headcount and whether there are co-organizers or a volunteer committee helping.

questions.title: Do you have a specific date and time in July in mind?
questions.description: Pin down the exact date to work backwards on deadlines for permits, vendors, and invitations.

questions.title: What is your total budget for the event?
questions.description: Identify the financial ceiling to guide all spending decisions across food, entertainment, and supplies.

questions.title: Have you looked into street closure permits for your area?
questions.description: Determine whether a permit is needed and where the party is being held — street, park, or private space.

questions.title: What overall vibe or theme are you going for?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a family-friendly cookout, a themed celebration, a casual gathering, etc., to shape tone and activity choices.

questions.title: What would make this event feel like a success to you?
questions.description: Identify the user's top priority outcome — strong turnout, community bonding, fun for kids, smooth execution — to guide task prioritization.
